The Jurassic Coast: 185 Million Years in 95 Miles

Dorset's Jurassic Coast is England's only natural World Heritage Site, and riding it by motorcycle is a brilliant experience. The coastline stretches from Orcombe Point in East Devon to Old Harry Rocks in Dorset, covering 95 miles of dramatic geology, fossil-rich cliffs, and quintessentially English seaside towns.

The Route

Start at Lyme Regis, the fossil capital of Britain, and head east. The coast road passes through Charmouth, Bridport, and the remarkable Chesil Beach — an 18-mile bank of shingle that connects the Isle of Portland to the mainland. Continue through Weymouth to Lulworth Cove and Durdle Door, then finish at Studland and the Old Harry Rocks.

Key Stops

  • Lyme Regis — Iconic harbour, fossil hunting on the beach, The Cobb harbour wall
  • Golden Cap — England's highest point on the south coast, walk from Seatown
  • Abbotsbury — Swannery, subtropical gardens, thatched village
  • Chesil Beach — Extraordinary geological feature, Portland viewpoint
  • Lulworth Cove — Perfect horseshoe bay carved from the chalk
  • Durdle Door — Natural limestone arch, one of England's most photographed landmarks
  • Corfe Castle — Dramatic ruined castle on a hill, classic English scene

The Riding

Dorset's roads are gentle rather than dramatic. The B3157 from Bridport to Weymouth follows the coast closely and offers good sea views. Inland, the A35 through Dorchester and the A351 to Corfe Castle are flowing main roads. The real joy is in the minor roads — narrow lanes through the Purbeck Hills and the rolling fields behind the coast.

The Jurassic Coast is best enjoyed at a leisurely pace. Stop often, walk to the cliff edge, and remember that the rocks beneath your wheels are 185 million years old.

Combining with Other Routes

The Jurassic Coast connects perfectly with the New Forest to the east (via the Sandbanks ferry from Studland) and Devon to the west. A three-day tour could cover Dartmoor, the Jurassic Coast, and the New Forest — three very different landscapes linked by excellent roads.

Practical Information

The Jurassic Coast is busy in July and August, especially around Lulworth and Durdle Door. Visit in May, June, or September for the best experience. Fuel and facilities are plentiful throughout Dorset. The area is accessible from London (2.5 hours via M3/A31), Southampton (1 hour), and Bristol (2 hours). Accommodation in Lyme Regis, Weymouth, and Swanage books up fast in summer. Read our Best Motorcycle Roads in Scotland: 15 Must-Ride Routes guide for more. Read our Norfolk Coast Motorcycle Route: England's Forgotten Shore guide for more.

faq.q: How long is the Jurassic Coast route?
faq.a: The coastline covers 95 miles, stretching from Orcombe Point in East Devon to Old Harry Rocks in Dorset. It is England's only natural World Heritage Site, spanning 185 million years of geology. Start at Lyme Regis, the fossil capital of Britain, and head east through Charmouth, Bridport and Chesil Beach to Weymouth, Lulworth Cove, Durdle Door and finally Studland.

Gentle rather than dramatic. The B3157 from Bridport to Weymouth follows the coast closely with good sea views, while inland the A35 through Dorchester and the A351 to Corfe Castle are flowing main roads. The real joy lies in the minor roads, the narrow lanes through the Purbeck Hills and the rolling fields behind the coast, so ride at a relaxed pace.

faq.q: When should I visit to avoid crowds?
faq.a: The coast is busy in July and August, especially around Lulworth Cove and Durdle Door. Visit in May, June or September for the best experience, with quieter roads and easier parking. Accommodation in Lyme Regis, Weymouth and Swanage books up fast in summer, so reserve ahead if you plan an overnight during the peak months.

faq.q: Can I combine it with other routes?
faq.a: Yes. The Jurassic Coast connects neatly with the New Forest to the east via the Sandbanks ferry from Studland, and with Devon to the west. A three-day tour could take in Dartmoor, the Jurassic Coast and the New Forest, three very different landscapes linked by excellent roads, making a superb long weekend from the south of England.

faq.q: How accessible is Dorset by bike?
faq.a: Very accessible. The area is roughly 2.5 hours from London via the M3 and A31, one hour from Southampton and two hours from Bristol. Fuel and facilities are plentiful throughout Dorset, so there is no need for careful range planning. It makes an easy weekend from much of southern England without a long slog to reach the good riding.
